tasks.short: Organize flight and traffic-management plans for incoming aircraft

steps.what: Read actual incoming flight plans, traffic-management plans and expected entry information for the assigned airspace
inputs: actual accepted flight plans and traffic-management plans
actual expected entry times/points and assigned airspace

steps.what: Determine the relevant incoming-flight order, dependencies and preparation needs for the actual traffic situation
inputs: controller-read incoming-flight planning information
actual traffic situation and operational constraints

steps.what: Organize the actual flight-plan or traffic-management-plan workspace and check the completed arrangement
inputs: controller's actual incoming-traffic organization decisions
controller-read incoming-flight planning information

steps.what: Save the completed checked incoming-plan arrangement in the existing planning workspace
inputs: complete checked incoming-plan arrangement

tasks.design: Configure an existing native incoming-flight view in {OTHER}, the air-traffic flight-plan workspace, to group actual accepted plans by the assigned sector and expected entry. The controller interprets the situation and organizes the real plans, checks the completed arrangement and saves it; no sequence or clearance decision is automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated plan navigation can accompany preparation for incoming traffic.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native filters can expose the accepted plans for the actual sector.
tasks.still_hard: Plan order alone does not resolve actual traffic conflicts or changing entry conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Prepare for the real traffic situation using operational judgment.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native flight-plan filters can reduce navigation while controllers retain traffic interpretation and actual plan organization.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. OTHER means existing operational flight-plan/traffic-management software.
Existing flight-planning services supply actual flight identity, accepted plan version, sector and expected entry point/time. Missing/conflicting fields require manual operational handling.
Only navigation changes. Plan organization and final checking are fully retained; an equivalent existing native view removes the gain.
Gross provisional saving 1.5 minus 0.5 hour of approved-view upkeep gives 1 net. Save is negligible and fully retained; no clearance or external plan send is proposed.
unknowns: Installed approved views and current navigation effort
research_questions: Does the actual native incoming-plan view remove repeated access actions without changing operational decisions?

already_counted.description: Read the actual incoming-flight planning information

incremental.description: Check sector/entry filter configuration after approved changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 1%; all traffic interpretation and actual organization remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile actual flight information from plans, reports and observations

steps.what: Read the actual flight plan, pilot reports, radar information and observations for the identified flight
inputs: actual flight identity and accepted flight plan
actual pilot reports, radar information and controller observations
outputs: controller-read flight evidence with source/time context

steps.what: Compile and reconcile the actual flight information and check identity, source time and disagreements in the completed record
inputs: controller-read flight evidence with source/time context
actual existing flight-record fields

steps.what: Save the completed checked flight-information record in the existing operational workspace
inputs: complete checked flight-information record

tasks.design: Configure native flight-context views and reuse of already-linked plan fields in {OTHER}, the operational flight-information system. The controller reads actual reports/observations, reconciles conflicts and completes the checked record before saving; no language model extracts or resolves operational meaning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing flight data can require repeated navigation and fixed-field entry during compilation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source links and plan-field reuse can reduce that repeated handling.
tasks.still_hard: Reports and surveillance can disagree or describe different times and flight identities.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve what the actual evidence means for the identified flight.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing flight-context views and linked plan fields can reduce navigation and entry while controllers reconcile actual reports and observations.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. OTHER means existing flight-information and surveillance systems.

Planning services supply actual accepted plan fields with flight identity/version/time. Pilots supply actual reports; surveillance and the controller supply actual observed data. No structured pilot-report feed is invented.
Only already-structured plan fields are reused; voice reports/visual observations are captured and checked manually inside s1/s2. Missing links or identity conflicts stop prefill.
Gross provisional saving 9.9 minus 1.5 hours of source/field mapping upkeep gives 8.4 net. Existing equivalent reuse removes the gain.
The record save remains negligible and fully retained; no clearance, external relay or automatic status conclusion is hidden in the design.
unknowns: Actual native field reuse and current manual compilation
research_questions: Which existing structured plan fields are still repeatedly entered in actual flight-information records?

already_counted.description: Read sources, capture unstructured reports and reconcile/check the complete record

incremental.description: Maintain approved source links and plan-field mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 8.4%; voice/visual capture and all conflict resolution remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Relay air-traffic information to control centers

steps.what: Read the actual aircraft course, altitude, expected arrival time and relevant operational context
inputs: actual flight-information and surveillance records
actual coordination need and intended control center
outputs: controller-read current information for the relay

steps.what: Determine the exact current flight information and intended center/flight identifiers to relay
inputs: controller-read current information for the relay
actual coordination procedures
outputs: controller-selected final traffic information and receiving center

steps.what: Relay the selected air-traffic information to the intended control center over the operational channel
inputs: controller-selected final traffic information and receiving center

tasks.design: Retain operational traffic-information relay with the controller using {OTHER}, the existing flight-information display and center-coordination channel. Source reading, exact information/recipient selection and the actual relay are separate; no new message automation is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: The relay must reflect actual current flight information and the receiving center's need.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing channels already support the communication; no new supported mechanism removes it.
tasks.still_hard: Flight identity, freshness and coordination meaning require operational judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Communicate the right current information to the right receiving controller.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: control-center relays require actual flight-information selection and operational communication.

assumptions: Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. OTHER means existing flight-information and center-coordination systems.
Existing flight/surveillance services supply actual information; missing or stale facts require manual operational handling. No new structured message feed is assumed.
The scenario is another center within the same organization, so the relay is write_internal; an external center would require act_external authority.
The final message and destination are chosen in s2 before transmission, without adding a separate approval ceremony. No record/report baseline is invented.
All work remains; gross/net saving are zero and no incremental upkeep is required.
unknowns: Actual center ownership and communication mechanism
research_questions: Does the actual approved coordination system offer a native feature that changes repeated relay work?

incremental.description: No new relay system or process proposed

approvals.approved_version: controller-selected final traffic information and receiving center

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No supported change to actual information reading, selection or operational relay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read actual weather, turbulence and other current flight-safety information relevant to the intended flight
inputs: actual intended flight context
current authorised weather, turbulence and flight-safety reports

steps.what: Determine the relevant conditions, suggested routes/altitudes and limitations to explain in the actual briefing
inputs: controller-read current briefing source information
actual flight context and applicable operational procedures
outputs: controller's actual briefing topics and operational advice

steps.what: Conduct the actual pre-flight briefing, explain conditions and suggestions and respond to the pilot's questions
inputs: controller's actual briefing topics and operational advice
pilot's actual questions and flight circumstances
outputs: actual pre-flight weather, route, altitude and safety briefing

tasks.design: Configure an existing native briefing-source view in {OTHER}, the approved weather/flight-information application, to expose current relevant reports together. The controller still interprets the flight context, chooses the advice and conducts the live briefing; no generated briefing or automatic route recommendation is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefing sources can require repeated navigation between current reports.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report views can group existing authorised information.
tasks.still_hard: Weather relevance, uncertainty and a pilot's actual flight circumstances require interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the useful implications and limits of the available flight-safety information.

ambition.what: No extra briefing capacity or automatic advice claimed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native briefing-source views can reduce report navigation while flight-context interpretation and live briefing stay with the controller.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. OTHER means approved weather/flight-information applications.
Existing authorised services supply actual timestamped reports; the actual flight context is supplied for the briefing. Missing or stale reports require normal operational handling.
Only source navigation changes; interpretation and the full live briefing remain. Existing equivalent views remove the gain.
Gross provisional saving 1.5 minus 0.5 hour of approved-view upkeep gives 1 net. No separate report, electronic send or clearance is introduced by this briefing design.
unknowns: Installed briefing views and current retrieval effort
research_questions: Can an approved native source view shorten real briefing report navigation while preserving full source checks?

already_counted.description: Read the actual current flight-safety sources

incremental.description: Check source-view links and current report availability

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 1%; all operational interpretation and live briefing remain unchanged.
